drhp.business: Jindal Poly Films was incorporated in 1974, started polyester yarn at Bulandshahr in 1985, and moved into BOPET film in 1996 and BOPP film in 2003. Through subsidiaries it now runs three businesses: packaging films (BOPP, BOPET, CPP, metallised, coated, thermal-lamination and capacitor films) made by JPFL Films Private Limited at Nashik; PP-based spunmelt and spunbond nonwoven fabrics for hygiene, healthcare and industrial uses; and a label business, Jindal SMI Coated Products Limited, with over 200 self-adhesive label products. It sells in domestic and international markets.

drhp.expansion: The report names no new capacity or expansion project. The packaging-films business is run by subsidiary JPFL Films Private Limited from its Nashik, Maharashtra plant, stated as 'BOPP total capacity 2,94,200 TPA, for BOPET total capacity 1,70,000 TPA, for CPP total capacity 33,600 TPA'. A fire at that plant (Village Mundhegaon, Igatpuri, Nashik) on 21 May 2025 caused a substantial loss of stock, fixed assets and infrastructure, and the company says it is working to revive operations. It gives no timeline or cost for the revival. The nonwovens business runs three Reicofil R5 and R4S multi-beam composite spunmelt (SSMMS) lines from Germany with a production capacity of 60,000 MT. The Ambernath MIDC label plant of Jindal SMI Coated Products has a solar installation that is expected to offset its energy consumption.

demand_drivers.title: Mdna (RHP)
demand_drivers.body:
- Indian flexible-packaging demand is growing at double digits, against a mid-single-digit global average. Management attributes this to low per-capita consumption, urbanisation, higher disposable incomes, organised retail and e-commerce.
- Demand for packaged goods is driven by food & beverages, pharmaceuticals, FMCG, personal care and e-commerce.
- Brand owners are moving to recyclable, mono-material packaging, which is opening room for sustainable and specialty films.
- The Indian film industry added more capacity during the year and the sector has excess capacity, which is pressuring prices and capacity utilisation. The company says it held its market share through its loyal customer base.
- Swings in PP and PET raw-material prices are a margin lever and a threat.
- Nonwoven demand is supported by hygiene awareness, expanding healthcare infrastructure and personal-care consumption, in both domestic and export markets.
- Label demand is driven by premium packaging, product-traceability requirements and a preference for pressure-sensitive labels in food, pharma, logistics and consumer goods.

capex_expansion.title: Expansion (RHP)
capex_expansion.body: The report names no new capacity or expansion project. The packaging-films business is run by subsidiary JPFL Films Private Limited from its Nashik, Maharashtra plant, stated as 'BOPP total capacity 2,94,200 TPA, for BOPET total capacity 1,70,000 TPA, for CPP total capacity 33,600 TPA'. A fire at that plant (Village Mundhegaon, Igatpuri, Nashik) on 21 May 2025 caused a substantial loss of stock, fixed assets and infrastructure, and the company says it is working to revive operations. It gives no timeline or cost for the revival. The nonwovens business runs three Reicofil R5 and R4S multi-beam composite spunmelt (SSMMS) lines from Germany with a production capacity of 60,000 MT. The Ambernath MIDC label plant of Jindal SMI Coated Products has a solar installation that is expected to offset its energy consumption.

moat.title: Strengths (RHP)
moat.body:
- scale: large packaging-film capacity at a single site — evidence: Nashik plant of subsidiary JPFL Films has BOPP total capacity 2,94,200 TPA, BOPET 1,70,000 TPA and CPP 33,600 TPA — against it: a fire at this Nashik plant on 21 May 2025 caused a substantial loss of stock, fixed assets and infrastructure, and the company is still working to revive operations; the MD&A also cites further capacity additions and excess capacity in the Indian film industry
- scale: multi-line spunmelt nonwoven capacity — evidence: three Reicofil R5 and R4S multi-beam composite spunmelt (SSMMS) lines from Germany with 60,000 MT production capacity

risks.title: Risks (RHP)
risks.body:
- The MD&A threats list says volatility in polypropylene and polyethylene terephthalate prices may hurt operating margins and profitability.
- Management says excess capacity may intensify competition, cause pricing problems and lower capacity utilisation across the sector. It also notes further capacity additions in the Indian film industry during the year.
- A faster shift to alternative sustainable packaging may cut demand for some conventional flexible-packaging products, forcing product innovation and portfolio changes.
- Stricter environmental rules could raise operating and capital spending and squeeze industry profitability.
- The MD&A and cautionary statement cite global trade uncertainties, changing consumer preferences, domestic and international economic conditions, and changes in government regulation and tax regime as factors that could change outcomes.

strategy.title: Strategies (RHP)
strategy.body:
- Revive operations at the Nashik packaging-film plant of subsidiary JPFL Films after the 21 May 2025 fire, which destroyed a substantial part of its stock, fixed assets and infrastructure.
- Spread the business beyond packaging films into PP spunmelt/spunbond nonwoven fabrics and, through Jindal SMI Coated Products, self-adhesive labels.
- Keep developing new products and improving quality across packaging films, nonwoven fabrics and labelling solutions.
- Label business: keep close ties with European and Asian suppliers to soften the impact of higher pulp and film-resin prices.

themes.title: Specialty packaging & sustainable materials
themes.need: Premiumization, e-commerce and a sustainability/recycling mandate drive a packaging up-cycle across flexible films, rigid plastics, cartons and compostables. UFLEX/EPL/HUHTAMAKI/COSMOFIRST/ESTER on films/tubes; TCPLPACK/AGI/BOROLTD on cartons/glass; MOLDTKPAC/MOLDTECH on rigid/IML; PAKKA/GANECOS on compostable & recycled materials.
themes.driver: Brand-owner restocking; export demand recovery; recycled-content mandates; commodity-cost pass-through.

hero.oneLiner: Holding company whose subsidiaries make BOPP, BOPET and CPP packaging films, PP-based spunmelt and spunbond nonwoven fabrics, and self-adhesive labels.
